title: Kill Goofy
location: Grove Street Theater, 130 Grove Street, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
Apricot Sky Productions’s new play, Kill Goofy by Livingston playwright Eric Alter, opens October 9 and plays for three weekends throught October 25. 
The story is simple on the surface. Two best friends, inseparable at thirteen, haven’t spoken in thirty years. One of them never left his childhood bedroom. His mother never left because someone had to take care of him. Then the other one comes back to town, and everyone in that house has been keeping the same secret. It’s a play about the things we never say to the people closest to us, and it sends people out the door talking. 
Please note the play deals with difficult subject matter and is recommended for ages 15 and up. The full synopsis and content advisory plus more information are at https://apricotskyproductions.com/killgoofy.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: FREE TOGETHER public event in Montclair on October 24
location: Church Street, Church Street, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Four local community organizations invite you to our public connection event on October 24, 10am–2pm, outdoors on Church Street in Montclair Center. 
We’re asking how we can all be FREE TOGETHER? – supporting one another in freedom, giving freely and joyfully to one another in our community, and expressing our needs freely and comfortably? 
Let’s open our imaginations – for a future where we have the freedom that comes from meeting one another’s needs within our community. 
Stop by for an interactive brainstorming and live art experience. Come meet local organizations already building community support systems! Learn about mutuality and mutual aid opportunities in our local area. We’ll listen to your ideas about community giving and receiving. 
Fun activities for adults and children will be offered. Free snacks too! 
• What could you imagine doing for or giving to your community – things that you enjoy so much that you wouldn’t want money to do them? 
• What do you have difficulty asking for help with? Help that you wish for, things you’ve been putting off, things big or small, for you or your family? 
FREE TOGETHER qr codeVolunteer artists will help us illustrate and express your ideas and imagination, for a collective visual collage of community members’ hopes, needs, desires, offers, and contributions – a vision of how we can be FREE TOGETHER. 
We don’t have all the answers. We’re inviting you to come brainstorm with us.

on mutuality and mutual aid
Saturday, October 24, 2026, 10am–2pm
(Rain date Sun Oct 25)

title: The Balanced Woman Blueprint:  Wellness Reset for Women 40+
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
RESET is a two-hour wellness experience designed for women 40+ who are ready to stop running on autopilot and start making intentional decisions about what comes next.


Saturday, October 24, 10am – 12noon, $45 
Get clear about what you want. Make bold decisions about what comes next. Leave with a practical plan to reclaim your life. 
You’ve spent years showing up for your career, your family, your relationships, and the people who depend on you. 
You’re capable. You’re responsible. You get things done. 
But somewhere along the way, you may have become the last person on your own list. 
And maybe you’re asking yourself: 

What do I actually want now?
What needs to change?
What do I want this next chapter to look like?Led by Sakirat Oladiran, NP, Board-Certified Nurse Practitioner and Certified Life & Health Coach, RESET combines guided reflection, meditation, meaningful conversation, and practical exercises to help you step back, get clear, and create a plan for moving forward.Your RESET Starts Here Reserve your seat today! 
Together, we’ll explore five areas that shape how you experience your life: 
BODY — Reconnect with your health, energy, and well-being.
MIND — Quiet the mental overload and create clarity.
JOY — Rediscover what makes you feel alive.
RELATIONSHIPS — Strengthen connections and create healthier boundaries.
PURPOSE — Get clear about what you want from this next chapter. 
You’ll Leave With: 
A clearer understanding of what you truly want
Greater confidence to make intentional decisions
Practical strategies for creating more balance
A personalized plan for your next steps
Renewed energy to move forward without losing yourself in the process 
This isn’t about adding more to your already-full plate. 
It’s about deciding what deserves a place on it. 
EVENT DETAILS 
Saturday, October 24 | 10:00 AM–12:00 PM
The Space • Montclair, NJ 

356 Bloomfield Ave, loft #2 and

5 S Willow St, second floor (there are 2 entrances) 
Food & beverages included
Intimate, interactive experience
Limited attendance 
Tickets: $45 + applicable Eventbrite fees 
Two hours. Five areas of your life. One opportunity to decide what comes next. 
You’ve invested in your career.
You’ve invested in your family.
You’ve invested in everyone around you. 
Now it’s time to invest in YOU. 
Come to RESET ready to reconnect with yourself—and leave ready to move forward. 
Reserve your seat today! 



The Space is located on the second floor of a historic building with no elevator.  Unfortunately we are unable to accommodate those with limited mobility.

title: Clean-Life Living
location: Union Congregational Church, 176 Cooper Avenue, Montclair NJ, 176 Cooper Avenue, Montclair, United States
description:
From Hip-Hop to Holistic Health: Clean-Life LIVING Brings Fresh Perspectives on Living Well to Montclair 
Darryl “DMC” McDaniels, Dr. Brian Clement, Warren Zanes and other notable guests come together October 24 for an afternoon of inspiration, connection and community benefiting Montclair Helps. 
MONTCLAIR, NJ — What do a hip-hop legend, a holistic wellness pioneer, a rock musician and bestselling author, a community builder and a scholar of American transcendentalism have in common? 
More than you might think. 
On Saturday, October 24, Montclair will host Clean-Life LIVING, an afternoon designed to explore what it means to live well in an increasingly complicated, demanding and often disconnected world. 
Taking place from 3:30 to 6:30 p.m. at Union Congregational Church, the event brings together an eclectic group of speakers whose experiences span music, nutrition, psychology, creativity, philosophy and community building. 
The theme is simple: Unplug. Reset. Integrate. 
And the underlying idea is that living well isn’t about finding one perfect diet, adopting a single wellness practice or following someone else’s prescription for a better life. It’s about taking a broader look at how we live—and becoming more intentional about integrating the things that help us flourish. 
“Clean-Life LIVING is about more than what we eat or the products we use,” explains the event’s organizing philosophy. “It’s about removing what gets in the way of feeling and living well—and making room for the practices that sustain us.” 
The afternoon will benefit Montclair Helps, a local nonprofit providing emergency financial assistance to neighbors facing unexpected crises. 
An Unlikely Gathering with a Common Purpose 
Among the featured guests is Darryl “DMC” McDaniels, co-founder of the groundbreaking hip-hop group Run-DMC. 
While McDaniels helped transform popular music and culture, his story extends far beyond the stage. His personal experiences with mental health challenges, self-discovery and his advocacy for children in foster care have made him an influential voice on resilience, belonging and purpose. 
In a conversation centered on Finding Your Voice & Your Purpose, McDaniels will share perspectives on navigating adversity, discovering authenticity and finding meaning through self-expression, human connection and giving back. 
Dr. Brian Clement, co-director of Hippocrates Wellness, brings a very different perspective. For more than five decades, Clement has advocated for plant-based nutrition, raw and living foods, and lifestyle-centered approaches to well-being. 
His presentation, Food as Medicine, will explore the relationship between what we eat, the habits we cultivate and our overall approach to health. Clement’s perspective invites attendees to reconsider the role that everyday nutritional choices can play in supporting well-being. 
Warren Zanes brings yet another dimension to the conversation: the power of creativity and the stories we tell about ourselves. 
A former guitarist with the rock band Del Fuegos, Zanes is also the bestselling author of Petty: The Biography and Deliver Me from Nowhere, his acclaimed exploration of Bruce Springsteen’s Nebraska album, which inspired the feature film about its creation. 
Drawing on his experiences as a musician, writer and storyteller, Zanes will explore creativity, generational trauma and the ways our personal narratives can either limit or expand our sense of possibility. 
His presentation, A Creative Life & Integrated Living, asks a compelling question: How might our lives change if we became more conscious of the stories that shape our identities? 
The Importance of Connection—and the Courage to Be Ourselves 
For Anjali Dalal, founder of Salonette, well-being is inseparable from human connection. 
A Yale Law School graduate and former attorney, Dalal began bringing people together through intimate gatherings in her own living room. Those experiences eventually inspired Salonette, an initiative centered on meaningful conversation, curiosity and community. 
In a conversation with Emily Kemeny-Rose, Dalal will explore how participation, openness and authentic relationships contribute to our sense of belonging—and why strengthening our connections may be one of the most important investments we can make in ourselves. 
The afternoon will also feature Barbara Solowey, a scholar of American transcendentalism and longtime educator who has spent decades teaching the works of Ralph Waldo Emerson, Henry David Thoreau, Walt Whitman and other influential American writers. 
Drawing on Emerson’s celebrated essay Self-Reliance, Solowey will consider the relevance of his ideas in contemporary life. 
What does it mean to trust our own judgment? How do we resist the pressure to conform? And how can we cultivate the courage to live more authentically? 
Her presentation, Emerson’s Self-Reliance in Everyday Life, will bring these timeless philosophical questions into the practical realities of modern living. 
Keeping the afternoon lively will be Craig Baldo, a Montclair comedian whose credits include Late Night with Conan O’Brien, Comedy Central and audience warm-up work for Last Week Tonight with John Oliver. Baldo will serve as host and master of ceremonies, bringing humor and energy to an afternoon that promises both reflection and entertainment. 
More Than Inspiration: Something to Take Home 
Although the speakers come from remarkably different backgrounds, the event’s organizers have invited each of them to work within a shared framework. 
Each will reflect on the experiences that shaped their perspective, connect their particular area of expertise to the broader picture of living well, and share insights that others might apply to their own lives. 
Importantly, speakers have also been encouraged to conclude with a practical invitation—a specific action, activity or practice that attendees can explore for themselves. 
The objective is not simply to leave people feeling inspired, but to help them translate that inspiration into everyday life. 
The idea of integration is central to the event. 
Nutrition, movement, sleep, emotional well-being, creativity, spirituality and human connection are often treated as separate pursuits. Clean-Life LIVING encourages attendees to consider how these dimensions of life intersect and reinforce one another. 
Sometimes living better means introducing a new practice. Other times it means recognizing something we’ve neglected, reconsidering an old assumption or simply becoming more conscious of what already matters to us. 
The organizers hope attendees leave with an expanded perspective, a renewed sense of possibility and at least one manageable step toward living more intentionally. 
Living Well. Helping Neighbors. 
Beyond the speakers and conversations, Clean-Life LIVING has another important purpose: supporting neighbors in need. 
The event is a fundraiser for Montclair Helps, a community nonprofit that provides direct financial assistance to individuals and families facing unexpected emergencies. 
Working through local nonprofit partners, Montclair Helps responds to urgent needs within 12 to 48 hours, providing one-time grants ranging from $200 to $2,000. 
The organization has already distributed nearly $300,000 in direct assistance, helping local residents navigate difficult moments when relatively modest financial support can make a meaningful difference. 
In that sense, the event’s message extends beyond individual wellness. 
Taking better care of ourselves, the organizers suggest, is connected to how we care for one another—and ultimately to the health and vitality of the community we share. 
It’s a fitting message for an event that brings together so many different voices under one roof. 
And perhaps that’s the larger point of Clean-Life LIVING: There is no single formula for living well. But there is much we can learn from one another. 
Event Information 
Clean-Life LIVING — Unplug. Reset. Integrate. 
Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026
Time: 3:30–6:30 p.m.
Location: Union Congregational Church, Montclair, NJ 
Featured guests: Darryl “DMC” McDaniels, Dr. Brian Clement, Warren Zanes, Anjali Dalal and Barbara Solowey. Hosted by Craig Baldo. 
Tickets: $45 in advance; $55 at the door. 
Beneficiary: Montclair Helps. All event donations received benefit people facing crises.
Tickets: https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/clean-life-living
More information: https://www.montclairhelps.org/
Attendees are encouraged to submit questions for the speakers in advance.

Writing the Body - A Writing Workshop for Women
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Writing the Body – A Writing Workshop for Women
What can poetry say about our bodies that ordinary language can’t? How can our bodily experiences open new paths for our writing? 
In this generative workshop for women and nonbinary writers, Barbara O’Dair – poet, writer, and cofounder of the Park St. Writers Series – leads the group through readings, discussion, and writing exercises, using prompts to reveal fresh language, unexpected stories, and adventurous forms, and drawing from subjects such as body image, sexuality, desire, gender, illness, health, and aging. 
After a short grounding exercise, we’ll read and discuss a few poems that use the body and bodily experience to create meaning and music. Then we’ll write short pieces from three or four prompts. Everyone is encouraged to read their work aloud, and if time allows, the poet can take a few questions about their piece from the group. 
After a five-minute break, the second half of the workshop is devoted to writing a poem or creative piece and reading it aloud — either within the group, or as a “test drive” for the open mic later that evening. 
A few of the prompts (we may not get to all of them): 

If Your Body Could Talk… What would it say? Write a monologue in which one part of your body finally gets a chance to speak.
The Inherited Body. Finish this sentence: “I inherited my [body/hair/teeth] from…” Your parent is a natural choice, but consider more surprising options too — neighborhood, gender, class.
Medical Chart. Write a list of notes about your body that might appear on a medical chart, from a doctor’s POV. Then write your version: what should we know about you and your body? What does your version tell us about you?
Your Body in Time. Meet your body at eight, 25, 48, and today (or, if you’re under 40, work out the right ages). Introduce your different bodies to each other. Maybe your 48-year-old body wants a word with your eight-year-old body. About what?

Writing the Body – A Writing Workshop for Women 
Saturday, October 24, 4:30 – 6:30, $44 – price includes admission to the open mic.   
Workshop participants will be invited to read their work at the Space for Words open mic for writers that will follow the workshop later the same evening at 8pm.  The first portion of the open mic will be for workshop participants, and the second half is open to all women and female identifying persons. 
Learn more about the open mic here. 
 
Barbara O’Dair is a poet, writer, and cofounder of the Park St. Writers Series based in Montclair, NJ.

title: The Space for Words Open Mic — Women's Edition
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
The Space for Words Open Mic — Women’s Edition
Doors 7:30 · Start 8 PM · $10 for everyone 
Our monthly open mic returns for a special edition dedicated to women and female-identifying writers. 
The first portion of the night belongs to the workshop that is held before the open mic. Barbara O’Dair will lead a writing workshop that presents the theme ‘if your body could talk’.  Learn more about the workshop here.  Participants come up to read what they wrote that afternoon – new work, still warm, out loud for the first time. If you spent the evening writing about your body, this is where it gets to be heard. 
The second portion is open to all women and female-identifying persons. Bring your poetry, short stories, or excerpts from your latest work – the stage is yours. The Space is a safe place to try out new material, read old favorites, experiment with a different genre, and even to sing a song if inspiration strikes you. Put your name in the basket on your way in and you’ll get a shot at the mic, with a maximum of 5 minutes. Depending on how many people sign up and if time allows, we can have people come up a second time. 
Come for the words, stay for the community. The Space for Words has grown into an amazing community of writers supporting one another, and this night is about turning that room over to women’s voices for an evening. All levels, all genres — fiction, non-fiction, memoir, poetry. Afterward we take time to socialize and vibe with one another. 
You don’t have to do both. Come for the workshop, come for the open mic, or make a night of it. 

Good to know
Audience members are, as always, a welcome and vital part of these performances. 
If you have published books you’d like to sell, bring some copies and be prepared to accept payment. 
General guidelines: 

Hate speech of any kind is never allowed and will be shut down.
Violence or references to physical harm to others will be shut down.

BYOB is welcome, and some light snacks and drinks are served. 
Accessibility: The Space is located on the second floor of a historic building, accessible via a flight of stairs. Unfortunately, there is no elevator access at this time. This means we are unable to accommodate wheelchairs or guests with significant mobility challenges. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

title: Susquehanna Super Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
It's been a long time since we've done a more difficult hike like this, but it's been a long time coming.
Since the son is going to "Trunk or Treat" with his mom, it is an opportunity to complete the final difficult section of the Conestoga Trail, as well as the next bit of the Mason-Dixon Trail in our rebooted series that we'd put on hold.
This promises to be challenging, but also very rewarding with views, history, and more.
After meeting at Pequea boat launch, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to our start point north of the Norman Wood Bridge.
We'll follow the Mason-Dixon Trail up to an overlook, and then down through a scenic gorge with small waterfalls. We then get on the towpath of the old Susquehanna and Tidewater Canal to Lock 12. This is the southern terminus of the Conestoga Trail.
We'll follow the Conestoga Trail across Norman Wood Bridge, and then up though lands to the north. Undulating terrain and beautiful vistas are throughout the section.
Pinnacle Rock and House Rock are among the best views on the entire trail. We'll also pass through lovely Tucquan Glen, and pass the Wind Cave, largest tectonic cave east of the Mississippi.
Those wanting more terrain and a bit more of a challenge than the other more recent hikes are going to love this one.
There are no food stops along the way. In fact, other than Norman Wood Bridge and two access roads, we won't even be crossing any roads on this one.
Distance will be normal, just over 15 miles. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: Marking Movement: A Journey Through 5Rhythms and Intuitive Painting
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Marking Movement: A Journey Through 5Rhythms and Intuitive Painting
Sayrah Garrison and Naz Botas | October 25 | 1 – 3:30 pm | The Space | $55 — 12 spots available 
The Space invites you to give expression to your movements through intuitive painting.  This is not creation from the level of thought, but rather from your inner intuition and guidance. 
Marking Movement brings together two powerful languages of self-expression – 5Rhythms movement meditation and intuitive painting – into one continuous, embodied experience. 
The 5Rhythms Practice
Created by Gabrielle Roth, 5Rhythms is a conscious dance practice rooted in the principle that when we put the psyche in motion, it can begin to heal itself. The five rhythms – Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness – each offer a different quality of movement and energy, helping us cultivate grounded bodies, clear minds, and inspired spirits. 
Guided by the 5Rhythms map, we’ll take a deep dive into our own inner landscape, moving beyond choreography and expectations to reconnect with our authentic selves. As we become more present in our bodies, we create space to listen more deeply to what is moving through us, including the art that wants to emerge. 
From Movement to Mark-Making
We’ll move through the session in cycles: approximately ten minutes of dance followed by ten minutes of painting, repeating as we travel through the five rhythms. Rather than stopping to think about what to paint, you’ll carry the energy and sensation of each rhythm directly from the dance floor to the wall, allowing your hands to express what your body has just discovered. 
And there’s a twist: none of the paintings belong to just one person. 
All twelve stations – each one ready with its own large sheet of paper taped to the wall, along with colored chalk pastels, charcoal, tempera paint, brushes, and pencils – are shared by the whole group. Throughout the class, everyone moves from station to station, adding their mark to artwork others have already begun. 
By the end, twelve collaborative paintings will emerge, each one holding traces of the collective movement, energy, intuition, and presence of the entire group. There is no need to finish “your” piece and no ownership to protect. Instead, the paintings become a visual conversation, like the way we dance with one another.  One person’s Chaos layered over another’s Flowing, one moment of Stillness resting beside someone else’s Lyrical expression – it will all result in works of beauty. 
This is an opportunity to bring our deepest prayers to life through conscious movement and intuitive art, while experiencing the creative energy that emerges when we move and make in community. 
No dance experience or art experience is required.  Just bring a willingness to move without choreography and paint without a plan. Come ready to get out of your head, into your body, and onto the wall. 
What to Expect
Five rounds of 5Rhythms-inspired movement, each followed by ten minutes of free, intuitive painting at a shared station. All art supplies are provided. 
Wear comfortable clothing that allows you to move freely and that you don’t mind getting a little paint on. 
Space is limited to 12 participants to keep the experience intimate and the twelve shared paintings feeling personal and alive. 
Meet Your Facilitator
Sayrah Garrison is an accredited 5Rhythms teacher who lives and works in Northern New Jersey. She has been dancing the 5Rhythms since 2001 and teaching since 2014. A social worker and mother, Sayrah is passionate about the healing arts and the transformative potential of movement, creativity, and community. 
Join us for this unique wellness experience — a space to move, listen, create, and discover what wants to flow through you.

title: Kill Goofy
location: Grove Street Theater, 130 Grove Street, Montclair, 07042, United States
description:
Apricot Sky Productions’s new play, Kill Goofy by Livingston playwright Eric Alter, opens October 9 and plays for three weekends throught October 25. 
The story is simple on the surface. Two best friends, inseparable at thirteen, haven’t spoken in thirty years. One of them never left his childhood bedroom. His mother never left because someone had to take care of him. Then the other one comes back to town, and everyone in that house has been keeping the same secret. It’s a play about the things we never say to the people closest to us, and it sends people out the door talking. 
Please note the play deals with difficult subject matter and is recommended for ages 15 and up. The full synopsis and content advisory plus more information are at https://apricotskyproductions.com/killgoofy.

Classic Films Now: All the President’s Men
description:
Run Time: 140 minutes. Recommended for ages 13+. 
A nation distrusts its institutions. News has become spectacle. Ordinary people fight to matter. Welcome to 1976. 
Academy Award winners Robert Redford and Dustin Hoffman star in this true story as Washington Post reporters Carl Bernstein and Bob Woodward, whose investigation of a seemingly minor hotel room break-in uncovers the greatest political scandal in United States history and leads to the downfall of President Richard Nixon. 
 
Classic Films Now brings major works of cinema back to the big screen, films that not only defined their own time but continue to speak to ours. Each installment of the series gathers a group of landmark films curated around a theme, period, artist, or movement, inviting audiences to discover how the works connect with contemporary life. 
This fall, Classic Films Now kicks off with a three-film series devoted to 1976, a remarkable year in American cinema and a revealing moment in the nation’s cultural imagination. Released in the shadow of Watergate, Vietnam, urban crisis, and the Bicentennial, All the President’s Men, Network, and Rocky offer three sharply different portraits of American life at a time of great transition and uncertainty. 
Screenings will be introduced and hosted by Rafer Guzmán. Rafer writes about movies, music, and popular culture for Newsday. He has been a film critic for WNYC, a co-host of the independent podcast “Movie Therapy,” and a staff writer at The Wall Street Journal.

title: October Writers Workshop at Watchung Booksellers
location: watchung booksellers the kids’ room, 44 Fairfield St., Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Watchung Booksellers hosts a writers’ workshop for creatives who are stuck in their process with therapist Amos Kamil on Sunday, October 25 afrom 6:00 – 8:00 p.m. 
Stuck isn’t a discipline problem. Most workshops on creative block treat it as a craft problem — outline more, write badly on purpose, lower the stakes. Useful, but it treats the symptom. As a therapist who works with writers and creative people, Amos Kamil goes one layer deeper: block is usually not a craft failure, it’s a psychological pattern doing its job (protecting against exposure, failure, an old judgment) and it responds to different tools than craft advice does. 
The workshop’s promise: leave having identified your specific sabotage pattern and practiced one concrete tool against it, live. In this introductory workshop, you’ll leave with: 
*A named pattern (your own version of the “quiet agent” derailing you)
*One practiced tool you can use again unassisted
*A one-line diagnosis of where your current project is stuck in the larger arc, not just “stuck” 
Tickets are $80 for the two-hour introductory workshop. Purchase at watchungbooksellers.com.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: 2026 Class Gift Tabling - Information and Philanthropy Cord Pick-Up
description:
Each year, our graduating class participates in a proud Class Gift tradition where members of the class invest in the University by supporting areas of Montclair State University that are most important to them. We invite the Class of 2026 to come together to show your support!
All gifts to Montclair count! Make your gift to any area of campus you feel most passionate about – such as the Emergency Book Fund, The Red Hawk Pantry, your school or college, The Fund for Montclair State or athletic program.
Your gift will pay it forward for future Red Hawks and kick-start your philanthropic connection to Montclair.

Commemorate your class year! Make a gift of at least $20.26 and you’ll receive your customized philanthropy cord to wear over your commencement robe. 
For a gift of $40, celebrate this milestone with your family, friends and colleagues by having your message displayed on the screen at the Commencement you will be participating in, and receive a customized philanthropy cord.

How do I get my customized philanthropy cord?
Customized philanthropy cords will be available for pick-up:

Monday, October 26 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Thursday, November 2nd  from 2:00 – 4:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Tuesday, December 8 in the Student Center Lobby

Graduates can also arrange to pick up their philanthropy cords in the Overlook Corporate Center, 150 Clove Road, Little Falls, NJ during business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Philanthropy cords can also be mailed to those who cannot pick it up. Please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving at stewartj@montclair.edu or 973-655-5328 to finalize options to get your cords for the Winter Commencement.
Every student has benefitted from donor generosity to areas of academic support, emergency funding for students and overall priorities to boost students’ success every day. Thank you for paying it forward!For more information, please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving, at 973-655-5328 or stewartj@montclair.edu.

title: Stronger Montclair Election Conversation
description:
Stronger Montclair is hosting a conversation at Montclair Public Library. Join us as neighbors and friends to discuss some of the issues facing the Township Council within the context of the Strong Towns Movement as we approach Election Day.

We plan to share a respectful conversation between residents of Montclair, in which participation is encouraged, to discuss issues such as the spiraling cost and the shortage of housing, shuttles and local transportation, parking and curbside management, safe streets for all users, and a sustainable, transparent local government finance.

This is not a structured debate or forum, rather an opportunity for individuals to be heard. The Township Council candidates are invited to participate as residents, with the same time constraints as everybody else. As we conclude, we’ll allow each candidate in attendance to make a statement limited to three minutes.

Registration is not required but recommended for event updates.

title: "All Over the World": The Geography of Rock, Jazz and More
location: Montclair Main - Conference Room, Montclair Public Library
description:

The presentations combine music, maps, musicians, narratives and memories!

Paul will highlight his travels to Memphis, Tenn.: Hamburg, Germany; Hawthorne, Calif.; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; Central Avenue in Los Angeles; Abbey Road in London; La Caverne de la Huchette in Paris; Clarksdale, Miss.; West 70th Street in New York; S. Michigan Avenue in Chicago, Il; W. Rampart Street in New Orleans; Tupelo, Miss, Grand Boulevard in Detroit; Cleveland; Liverpool, England; the 9th Ward of New Orleans, 9137 S. Figueroa in Los Angeles--and more.

title: The Assembly of Lovers - Sufi Drum Circle
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
This will be the last one in the current Space until the new location is ready.  November and December circles will be held at the Quaker House on Park St. 
Community drum and chant circle rooted in Sufi prayer. 
Meets every other Monday:  October 12, October 26, etc. 
Contribution: Sliding scale donation $20–$40 (no one will be turned away) 
This is a vibrant Community Drum and Chanting Circle, where we drum and chant from our hearts into the universe. This experience is open to absolutely everyone, regardless of background or belief system—all that’s required is an open heart and a willingness to connect through sound.  The term ‘lover’ in this context refers to seekers on the Sufi path who are longing for union with the divine energy.  You can think of this gathering as an expansion of the sema sufi meditations we used to offer.  It is looser in form, more focused on music, and does not necessarily involve whirling, although it is welcome if you are called to it. 
There is a rhythm older than thought. A pulse that moves beneath language, beneath belief, beneath the self that thinks it’s separate. The Mystics knew this. The Sufis practiced it in Majalis al-‘Ushshāq. The Assembly of Lovers. Not lovers of ideas. Not lovers of comfort. Lovers magnetized by the Beloved. Those who’ve tasted the Divine Honey and cannot forget. Whose hearts remember what the mind has been taught to ignore. This is a gathering for those who feel the pull. The Assembly of Lovers meets twice each month, a rhythm of remembrance. Each gathering deepens the last. The circle becomes a living pulse of devotion. If you have a drum, bring it. Medicine drums, frame drums, and ceremony drums are all welcome. The circle grows stronger when every heartbeat joins the rhythm. 
The Flow 
Opening (5 minutes)
We set intention. A short prayer to open the way. To align the heart toward what is Real. 
Chanting and Rhythm (30-40 minutes)
Using the Sufi Chants of the Heart as a guide (our vision is for the chants to grow to what the individuals in the circle are inspired to invoke), we share simple chants. The drum holds the pulse. The voice follows. The meanings are offered, not explained. 
Repetition is the technology. The heart softens through return. Through invoking the Divine until the one invoking dissolves. 
Silent Resting (5-10 minutes)
After the chanting, we sit. No guidance. No instruction. 
The echo of the words and rhythms settles. The heart rests in what was touched. 
Closing (5 minutes)
A prayer of Unity. Of Oneness. We complete the circle and return to silence. 
Gratitude for what was offered. For what was received. 
  
Who This Is For 
This is for those who’ve felt the pull and don’t know what to call it. 
For those tired of spiritual talk that never touches the ground. 
For those who suspect that the heart knows a language the mind cannot translate. 
For those who long. 
Not for something. Not for someone. 
Just longing itself. The flame that keeps you moving toward what you cannot name but cannot forget. 
Osama Janakat 
 
Osama studied Mathematics and Physics at Rutgers University, laying a foundation of analytical thinking that complements his creative pursuits. As a beat-maker and music producer, he explores the intriguing connections between music, philosophy, and spirituality. 
Born in Jordan with Circassian roots, Osama’s move to the US in 2004 sparked a journey of inner exploration and spiritual discovery. An avid student of the Sufi tradition, he continues to seek wisdom that bridges cultures and disciplines, finding harmony in the interplay of art and spirituality.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

The Essex-Passaic Chapter of NAMI (The National Alliance on Mental Illness) Connection Recovery Peer Support Group Program meets on the 4th Tuesday of each month at the West Caldwell Library on 30 Clinton Road. 

NAMI is the most influential organization devoted to helping people with mental illness and their relatives and loved ones recover and deal with mental health issues. These meetings will be led by people having some form of mental illness. During these meetings, we will conduct peer support though all people interested in this organization are encouraged to attend. You do not have to sign up in advance. All meetings are kept confidential and are led by people specifically trained to conduct these meetings.

 NAMI Connection is a recovery peer support group program that offers respect, understanding, encouragement and hope. NAMI Connection groups are:

·       Free and confidential

·       Held monthly for 90 minutes  

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.  

 

https://nami.org/Home

title: Documentary Film Screening: Becoming Benjamin Lay
description:
Please join the English and History students and faculty from the course Radical New Jersey to watch this new, limited release documentary on Benjamin Lay, Quaker rebel, early abolitionist, and New Jersey’s most radical son.  
6:30pm, Thursday, October 27 in Dickson Hall 176. 
More information: In 1738, the four-foot Benjamin Lay famously stabbed a bible full of fake blood at a Quaker meeting, decades before abolition became a cause. He lived in a cave in Burlington County, was expelled from every Quaker meeting he entered, but refused to stop. In this documentary, actor Mark Povinelli adapts his one person show “The Return of Benjamin Lay” for a performance before the Little People of America conference in Baltimore in 2024. Permission to screen this documentary comes courtesy of the playwright, historian, and producer Marcus Rediker. 
Everybody is welcome!

Hosted by: College of Humanities and Social Sciences (CHSS)

title: Tuesday Night Open Studio Figure Drawing
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
This is the last one for a couple of weeks until the new Space location is ready!  This will be a party so bring some snacks and drinks… and charcoal, paint, paper, etc… 
Tuesdays, 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space | All skill levels welcome 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in person. 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. 
Each week a different model – usually nude, and sometimes clothed – serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say, observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a supportive community of seekers, artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies – charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. 
Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Mapping the Election: The Impact of Historic and Modern Maps on the Midterms NEW
location: Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - Kids Place, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

All eyes are on the midterm elections, and maps--both old and new--not only show how people vote but often help set and reinforce the patterns of how citizens are divided. First we'll take a look at maps of gerrymandering, which started in Massachusetts in 1811 and have taken very specific forms in the United States because of the rules of the American political system. We'll move onto the familiar red and blue election maps and examine how they privilege big, sparsely populated states like Wyoming over dense locations like New Jersey. We'll also take quick looks at great historical images, like Civil War-era election maps whose sectional splits look shockingly modern.

In each class, we'll consider one element of fiction or creative non-fiction, such as point of view, narrative voice, and what makes a piece of writing riveting, or boring. Students can expect in-class writing prompts, reading aloud, and optional homework. Positive encouragement, rather than formal critiques, will be featured, and inspiration and organization for writers will be discussed. Students should bring whatever they use to write to each class.

title: (CXLD) Home Repair Essentials
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. 

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Building Your Financial Roadmap: A Financial Wellness Series
location: Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - First Floor, Montclair Bellevue Avenue Branch
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Take control of your financial future with this four-part financial wellness workshop series designed to help you build a stronger foundation for making informed money decisions. Each workshop focuses on a practical aspect of financial wellness, from understanding how money grows and creating a plan for where your money should go, to preparing your family and planning for retirement.

Whether you're just getting started, looking to strengthen your financial habits, or preparing for the future, you'll gain practical knowledge, useful tools, and actionable strategies you can apply to your own financial life.

Each week we'll answer one important question about your financial future:


	
	How does money grow?
	



	
	Where should my money go first?
	



	
	How do I prepare my family for the future?
	



	
	How do I prepare myself for retirement?
	


Whether you attend one workshop or the entire series, you'll leave with practical knowledge and actionable steps to help you make informed financial decisions.

These workshops are for educational purposes only and are intended to provide general financial education. They should not be considered individualized financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.

title: Eagle Rock Reservation
description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

We will hike for about an hour - 3.5 miles. We will be walking on trails in the woods, so appropriate footwear, long pants & socks, and bug spray.

Will will meet at:
[https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7](https://goo.gl/maps/7rRRTiXCntdE1neD7) Eagle Rock Trail Parking Lot by Kiosk#1

If you enter from Eagle Rock Way, go pass the Highlawn and stay left. There will be a parking lot at the end of the curve to your right.

Eagle Rock Reservation is 408 acres of hills, streams, and valleys located on the borders of West Orange, Verona, and Montclair, New Jersey. Though located in the middle of the most densely populated county in the most densely populated state in the country, the Reservation is mostly undeveloped and boasts an extensive trail system within its borders.

**Please make sure to RSVP and arrive 5 minutes prior to start time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Please note: the timing of Timing Option A will go back one hour from Sat Nov 7th onwards to 6AM PDT / 9AM EDT**

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**TRAIL WORK will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are making progress!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site. (Note: While we normally meet the first Sudnay of each month, this volunteer day was shifted after the Labor Day weekend.)

Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required though if you sign up on Meetup, it helps us know how many tools to bring.) Only heavy, steady rain cancels.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

👟 **Court Priority:** Those who are signed up and show up by 9 AM will have top priority for court space. Those who show up later have second priority while those who are wait-listed will have third priority. This is only in the event that we have to rotate people in.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: From Swastika to Jim Crow (2000): Screening and Discussion
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a free Adult School event. Registration is required.

Explore an influential, little-known chapter in the history of Black-Jewish relations in America. We'll be screening a documentary film, From Swastika to Jim Crow,  based on a book by the same title by Gabrielle Simon Edgcomb. It tells the story of German-Jewish refugees, who, expelled from their homeland by Hitler and the Nazis, found new lives and careers at historically Black colleges and universities in the American South, influencing a whole generation of Black students and professionals. After the screening, Dr. Lillie Johnson Edwards and Rabbi Julie Roth, will discuss the film's significance. Dr. Edwards is a Drew University Professor Emerita of History and African American Studies. Rabbi Roth leads Congregation Shomrei Emunah of Montclair, NJ.

This program is co-sponsored by Shomrei Emunah (https://shomrei.org/) and The Mark Montclair https://themarkmtc.org).

Frank Sole, Henry Nerenberg, Jay Wilensky, Darrell Courtley, and Jeff Rantzer are the regulars in the band.

title: Classic Films Now: Network
description:
Run Time: 121 Minutes. Recommended for ages 18+ 
A nation distrusts its institutions. News has become spectacle. Ordinary people fight to matter. Welcome to 1976. 
Best Picture nominee about a mentally unstable news anchor who, after being told he’s to be fired, becomes a media superstar when he begins delivering nightly rants and threatens an on-air suicide for his final broadcast. Paddy Chayevsky’s script won an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay; Peter Firth received a posthumous Best Actor award as the unhinged newsman; and Faye Dunaway won Best Actress as a scheming network exec. 
 
Classic Films Now brings major works of cinema back to the big screen, films that not only defined their own time but continue to speak to ours. Each installment of the series gathers a group of landmark films curated around a theme, period, artist, or movement, inviting audiences to discover how the works connect with contemporary life. 
This fall, Classic Films Now kicks off with a three-film series devoted to 1976, a remarkable year in American cinema and a revealing moment in the nation’s cultural imagination. Released in the shadow of Watergate, Vietnam, urban crisis, and the Bicentennial, All the President’s Men, Network, and Rocky offer three sharply different portraits of American life at a time of great transition and uncertainty. 
Screenings will be introduced and hosted by Rafer Guzmán. Rafer writes about movies, music, and popular culture for Newsday. He has been a film critic for WNYC, a co-host of the independent podcast “Movie Therapy,” and a staff writer at The Wall Street Journal.

title: 2026 Class Gift Tabling - Information and Philanthropy Cord Pick-Up
description:
Each year, our graduating class participates in a proud Class Gift tradition where members of the class invest in the University by supporting areas of Montclair State University that are most important to them. We invite the Class of 2026 to come together to show your support!
All gifts to Montclair count! Make your gift to any area of campus you feel most passionate about – such as the Emergency Book Fund, The Red Hawk Pantry, your school or college, The Fund for Montclair State or athletic program.
Your gift will pay it forward for future Red Hawks and kick-start your philanthropic connection to Montclair.

Commemorate your class year! Make a gift of at least $20.26 and you’ll receive your customized philanthropy cord to wear over your commencement robe. 
For a gift of $40, celebrate this milestone with your family, friends and colleagues by having your message displayed on the screen at the Commencement you will be participating in, and receive a customized philanthropy cord.

How do I get my customized philanthropy cord?
Customized philanthropy cords will be available for pick-up:

Monday, October 26 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Thursday, November 2nd  from 2:00 – 4:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby
Tuesday, December 8 in the Student Center Lobby

Graduates can also arrange to pick up their philanthropy cords in the Overlook Corporate Center, 150 Clove Road, Little Falls, NJ during business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Philanthropy cords can also be mailed to those who cannot pick it up. Please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving at stewartj@montclair.edu or 973-655-5328 to finalize options to get your cords for the Winter Commencement.
Every student has benefitted from donor generosity to areas of academic support, emergency funding for students and overall priorities to boost students’ success every day. Thank you for paying it forward!For more information, please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving, at 973-655-5328 or stewartj@montclair.edu.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Reclaiming Your Inner Wisdom: Sacred Indigenous Teachings with Asha Frost
description:
You must register here to attend:  https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/217344



In a fast-paced world that often leaves us feeling overwhelmed and disconnected, true healing does not come from looking outward—it begins within. Join us for a transformative virtual conversation with Indigenous Medicine Woman Asha Frost as she explores her groundbreaking book, You Are the Medicine: 13 Indigenous Teachings to Connect to Your Inner Wisdom, Reclaim Your Power, and Heal.

The Medicine you have been searching for lives within you. Follow the path of the 13 Ojibwe Moons with Animal Spirits and Ancestors as your guides as you unlock your connection to your own unique, inherent healing power. Through storytelling, ceremonies, and Shamanic journeys, learn to apply ancient wisdom to your life in ways that are respectful and conscious of the stolen lands, lives, and traditions of Indigenous peoples.

Discover how to:

- Ground and root into your own lineage and meet your Ancestral guides.
- Practice self-care and rest on your journey.
- Return to Ancestral ways of cleansing and purifying.
- Trust and surrender so you can manifest and thrive.
- Release self-doubt, fear, disconnection, and insecurity.

Register now and take the first step toward recognizing and reclaiming your innate wisdom. 

About the Author: 

Asha Frost (she/her) is an Indigenous Medicine Woman and a member of the Chippewas of Nawash First Nation. She is from the Crane Clan, the totem of leadership, and believes in holding space from vision and heart. As an energy healer, homeopath, and mentor, Asha has guided thousands of people through profound and lasting transformation.

Impacted by generational trauma and colonization, Asha has been on a lifelong journey of reclamation. A lupus diagnosis sent her on a path of studying and practicing a multitude of energy Medicine modalities with many guides. She has blended this life experience with her innate gifts and the wisdom of her Ancestors. She loves sharing her Medicine in powerful ways through Ceremonies, teachings, and speaking events. Through this work, she loves seeing people reclaim their roots, find their healing wisdom, and rise into their power.

Asha lives on Anishinaabe, Huron-Wendat, and Haudenosaunee Territory, with her husband and two beautiful children, with whom she co-creates a better world for the seven generations to come.

title: The American Experiment: Information, Power, and Democracy: The First Amendment
description:
Join President Koppell for his first lecture in the American Experiment series, where he will discuss Information, Power, and Democracy: The First Amendment.
The First Amendment is the cornerstone of American democracy because it guarantees the fundamental freedoms required for citizens to govern themselves, including freedom of speech, freedom of the press, and freedom of assembly.  Citizens need access to open debate, diverse viewpoints, and accurate information in order to make informed decisions. These freedoms also protect unpopular and minority opinions and act as a check on the state from censoring speech or controlling what people learn, think, and say.  This lecture examines the foundational freedoms of the First Amendment and how they are applied to contemporary American democratic life, including: the impact of money on expression, the role of new media and corporate media, the role of the press in investigating and disseminating information, the right to protest as a form of assembly and expression, and the challenges posed by misinformation, disinformation, polarization, fragmented media audiences, and declining public trust. At its center is a fundamental question for American democracy: What are the inherent rights and responsibilities of freedom of expression in a democratic society?

title: 5 Week Course: The Work on Inadequacy (Timing Option A) Price - Sliding Scale
description:
The Mindful Stream
To celebrate 5 years of The Work Runs Free, Emrys has created The Work on Inadequacy. Over 5 weeks, we explore different ways the experience of inadequacy shows up in our lives, using The Work to investigate our experience.

Sign up form: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeQVso7QaCu9ubv5E_74f50c6vvp2nt7zx8zMWnlGkwaNIYMw/viewform?usp=preview)
Detailed Course Outline: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eQYHU2jgRlNoO_XZDEjj08EhT8jeHk0h2zAOnEoglgM/edit?usp=sharing)

**Sliding Scale Price:** $120 — Accessible rate / $150 — Standard rate / $180 — Pay it forward

**Please note: the timing of Timing Option A will go back one hour from Sat Nov 7th onwards to 6AM PDT / 9AM EDT**

**Week 1 — I'm Not Good Enough:** The fundamental inadequacy story.
**Week 2 — Comparison:** Measuring ourselves against other people.
**Week 3 — I'm a Fraud / They'll Find Me Out:** Imposter feelings, competence and exposure.
**Week 4 — Being Loved, Accepted & Enough:** Inadequacy in relationships, belonging and being seen by others.
**Week 5 — Achievement & Where I Should Be:** Success, progress, potential and the feeling that we should be further along.

The course gently moves from the broader experience of inadequacy into increasingly specific areas where it can show up in our lives.

As we gently move into each topic, you are invited to become still and notice any stressful thought, belief or experience that arises through the inquiry, and to write it down — either on a notepad or in an electronic document.

Each session explores one stressful thought, or “one-liner,” using a format known as Popcorn Work. This is the same approach Emrys uses in his weekly *[The Work Runs Free](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/)* group. Everyone participates in their own inquiry, but there is no expectation to share. You are equally welcome to keep your inquiry entirely private, if that feels right for you.

The group is deliberately small, with a maximum of 10 participants, allowing us to explore together while each person remains connected to their own experience.

Please note that this is a paid course. In order to join you must register for the event (sign up form above). The Zoom link for this event will be sent around 24 hours after registration and payment has been made.

**To book a free introductory private session of The Work with Emrys, [click here](https://calendly.com/mindfulnesswithemrys/onehoursession)[.](https://mindfulnesswithemrys.business.site/)**

description:

Julia Strayer and Liz Maccarone will lead a lively and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio.

This is a virtual program that takes place over Zoom. As the date approaches, you will receive an email with the Zoom link.

About the Presenters

Julia Strayer, CPWA®, CIMA®, CRPC® Senior Vice President, Wealth Management Advisor.  Prior to joining Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2000, Julia was a vice president and private banker for BankBoston’s Private Bank for 7 years, responsible for asset management and trust services. Previously, Julia worked in marketing for 9 years with Merrill. Julia has a BA from Ohio State University and an MBA from New York University’s Stern School of Business. Julia has appeared on the CNBC show “Power Lunch,” CBS “This Morning,” WGCH’s “Women in Business,” in addition to featured articles in USA Today.

Liz Maccarone, CRPC® Senior Financial Advisor.  Liz joined Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2012. Liz works closely with high-net-worth individuals and their families to create personalized and comprehensive strategies that support their goals, including investment management, retirement planning, liability management, and multigenerational planning. Liz values the importance of establishing and cultivating relationships with families including the next generation. Liz graduated from Fairfield University with a dual bachelor’s degree in Finance and Marketing. She began her career working at a boutique investment firm as a Business Development Associate, specializing in commodities and futures trading.

description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

A workshop for anyone who wants to write or wants to infuse their existing writing practice with new energy. In each class, we'll consider one element of fiction or creative non-fiction, such as point of view, narrative voice, and what makes a piece of writing riveting, or boring. Students can expect in-class writing prompts, reading aloud, and optional homework. Positive encouragement, rather than formal critiques, will be featured, and inspiration and organization for writers will be discussed. title: (CXLD) Home Repair Essentials
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. 

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

description:
Join the West Caldwell Public Library in welcoming Bergen County NJ Author RoseMarie Rubinetti Cappiello;  Intuitive/Medium/Healer, Hospice Trained Grief Volunteer, Ordained Spiritual Minister, Certified Hypnotherapist, Yoga Instructor, Reiki Attuned, BS Physical Education MSU and Author of Speaking From Spirit. 

EVENT WILL TAKE PLACE AT THE TOWN HALL (30 CLINTON RD, 2ND FLOOR)

Do you feel connected to Spirit, higher intelligence– a consciousness greater than you? Do you actively call on this source for support to help you in your day to day life? What if you could access this creative force in a tangible, practical and authoritative way? We will discuss this often under-utilized resource and how to work with it in a more conscious and powerful way. We will call on and build our connection to our unseen helpers—who are always helping us anyway whether we believe in them or not- and build our success teams for health and wellness and for financial support, guidance, success, assistance and structure. We will call on the relationship specialists and even the ones for career guidance and direction. Just as there are people with special gifts and skills on Earth that can assist us- Higher Consciousness/Heaven is filled with such guides, teachers, helpers and angels that have specialties too. Come meet the teams, build the teams and work with the behind the scenes helpers that work with you. When you work consciously with your spirit teams you will notice that life just seems to work out easier. Things start falling into place miraculously. Details get ironed out and things come together in a perfect way. You will always be in the right place at the right time, meeting the right people and opportunities and resources show up in unexpected ways. This class can be taken over and over again to gain even more insight, help and support from spirit. This is truly life changing information. Please bring a notebook and pen.

Trained by the best teachers from Arthur Findlay College in England, RoseMarie has highly developed psychic, mediumistic, intuitive, healing abilities. She has worked professionally as a Medium/Intuitive/Healer since 2000 and has connected many people to their loved ones in Spirit through thousands of private medium readings and platform medium demonstrations throughout the United States. Many people claim their lives change dramatically after having a reading with her and that the weight of grief and sadness significantly decreases.

In addition, she is a Spiritual Teacher who teaches online classes in psychic-spiritual development and conducts live classes in many venues across the country. Some topics covered are Telepathy, Dream Interpretation, Psychic Studies, Mediumship Development and Understanding the Soul and Spirit.

She is also a regressionist who does private and group healing work and Other Life Regression (often referred to as Past Life Regression).

Through her hospice training she often works with people and their families as they are getting ready to transition. She feels completely privileged and blessed to do this work.

Lastly, she is an adjunct professor at Montclair State University NJ where she teaches yoga in the physical education department.
